contributes.description: What the extension adds to Irori, by contribution kind.

permissions.description: What the extension may access. Shown to the owner for approval at install.

ApiScope.description: Access to the Irori API beyond the extension's own devices and entities.

oneOf.description: Read every device, entity, area, and floor.
Subscribe to events, including state changes of every entity.
Call services on any entity, e.g. turn on a light another protocol provides.

Contributions.description: The `[contributes]` table: one list per contribution kind.

app.description: Reserved for Phase 3; read but ignored, with a warning.

automation.description:
Reserved: an automation engine. Read but ignored, with a warning, until a later Irori
implements the host.

card.description: Reserved for Phase 2c; read but ignored, with a warning.

dashboard.description: Reserved for Phase 2c; read but ignored, with a warning.

protocol.description: At most one per extension in this version (ROADMAP D25).

Description.description: A short description. 1-500 characters on one line, no leading or trailing whitespace.

EntityKind.description:
What an entity is. The kind is also the domain part of its [`crate::EntityId`] and the
prefix of its services (`light.turn_on`).

oneOf.description: On/off, e.g. a smart plug or relay.
A numeric or text reading, e.g. temperature or illuminance.
A two-state reading, e.g. motion or a door contact.

ExtensionId.description: Format of a slug (extension id): lowercase letters a-z and digits, in words separated by single `_`. 1-64 characters.

config_schema.description:
JSON Schema for the extension's settings, relative to the package root. External
extensions only: a built-in extension's schema comes from its Rust config type.

icon.description:
A square SVG, relative to the package root, shown beside the extension and its devices so
they can be told apart at a glance. Always displayed as an image, never inlined into a
page, so it can't run script. A built-in extension embeds the file as well
(`Protocol::ICON`).

id.description: Also the id of the protocol it contributes, if any (ROADMAP D25).

irori.description: Which versions of Irori it works with, e.g. `>=0.1.0, <0.2.0`.

HostPath.description: `$CONFIG`, `$DATA`, or an absolute path, optionally followed by `/`-separated names, e.g. `$CONFIG/rules` or `/home/pi`. Anything outside `$CONFIG` and `$DATA` means full access to the machine.

IotClass.description: Where a protocol's devices live and how it learns about changes (ROADMAP D24).

oneOf.description: On the local network; devices report changes as they happen.
On the local network; Irori asks for changes periodically.
Through a cloud service that reports changes as they happen.
Through a cloud service that Irori asks periodically.

Name.description: A human-readable name. 1-100 characters, no leading or trailing whitespace.

NetworkHost.description: An internet hostname, e.g. `api.example.com`, or `*.example.com` for every subdomain. Not an IP address or a local-network name (`.local`, `.home.arpa`, `.internal`, `.lan`, `.home`): those need `lan`.

PackagePath.description: A path relative to the extension package root, e.g. `bin/esphome`. Segments use letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-` and don't start with `.`.

Permissions.description:
The `[permissions]` table (ROADMAP D23). Everything defaults to "no access".

A protocol never needs a permission to manage its own devices and entities or to
receive service calls for them; these cover reaching anything beyond that.

api.description: Irori API access beyond its own devices and entities.

host_fs.description:
Files and folders on the machine. `$CONFIG` and `$DATA` are Irori's own folders; any
other path means full access to this machine.

host_shell.description: Run commands on the machine. Means full access to this machine.

lan.description: Devices on the local network: private and link-local addresses, and mDNS (`.local`).

network.description: Internet hosts it connects to, e.g. `api.switch-bot.com` or `*.example.com`.

ProtocolAction.description:
A UI-triggerable action a protocol declares — the other half of "dedicated add-device path
per protocol," alongside the passive `Waiting` list.

id.description: Its own id, unique within this protocol, e.g. `permit_join`.

seconds.description:
A default duration in seconds, for a timed action — a hint the UI can show (e.g.
"for 60s"), not enforced by the core.

ProtocolContribution.description: A `[[contributes.protocol]]` entry: the extension brings in devices and entities.

actions.description:
Actions the UI can trigger beyond passively finding devices (`docs/specs/protocols.md`
§5) — Zigbee's "permit joining," say. Empty for a protocol with nothing to trigger; this
only declares that an action exists, not that it's usable right now (the protocol says
that at runtime, `set_available_actions`).

entity_kinds.description: The kinds of entity it creates. It must handle the standard services of each kind.

iot_class.description: Where its devices live and how it hears about changes. Shown as a badge.

run.description: How to start it, for external extensions. Built-in extensions leave this out.

RunCommand.description: How the core starts an external extension's process.

command.description: The executable, relative to the package root, e.g. `bin/esphome`.

SerialPath.description: A serial or USB device path under /dev, e.g. `/dev/ttyUSB0`.

Version.description: Semantic version MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional -pre-release, e.g. 1.4.0 or 0.3.0-beta.1. No build metadata. At most 64 characters.
